title: Let callers of clone a node exclude descendants
body: HTML's selectedcontent element and SVG's use element clone a subtree and then remove elements from the copy. Cloning runs cloning steps and attribute change steps, and cloning a custom element enqueues an upgrade, so the elements that are removed afterwards can still fetch resources and run script. The new excludeDescendant argument lets them leave such elements out of the copy instead. It applies to the descendants of the node being cloned, including those in clonable shadow trees, but not to the node itself or to template contents. - [ ] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * WebKit: https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/81772 * … - [ ] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * This only adds a hook. https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13320 uses it for selectedcontent, which is tested by `html/semantics/forms/the-select-element/customizable-select/selectedcontent-does-not-clone-omitted-subtrees.html`, part of the WebKit PR above. - [ ] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: … * Gecko: … * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=332569 * Deno (only for aborting and events): N/A * Node.js (only for aborting and events): N/A - [ ] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: N/A, no web developer-facing change by itself. - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
